profile.summary: Bacformer Large is the larger of the two Bacformer sizes. Like the base size it treats a whole bacterial genome as a sequence of proteins ordered along the chromosome and plasmids, but it embeds each protein with ESM-C 300M and runs a 30-layer transformer of hidden size 960 over those per-protein vectors, returning an embedding for each protein that depends on the rest of the genome. Two checkpoints are released: bacformer-large-masked-MAG, pretrained on about 1.3 million metagenome-assembled genomes, and bacformer-large-masked-complete-genomes, which is listed for complete genomes and whose Hugging Face metadata gives bacformer-large-masked-MAG as its base model.

summary_quotes.text: A key member of this collection is **bacformer-large-masked-MAG**, a 300M-parameter base transformer model trained on ~1.3M diverse metagenome-assembled genomes across more than 20k bacterial species and multiple environments.
The transformer is 30 layer transformer with `hidden_dim=960` and is trained from scratch.
A 300M parameter model pretrained on the ~1.3 M metagenome-assembled genomes (MAG) with a masked objective, randomly masking 15 % of the proteins.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: Each protein of a genome is embedded with ESM-C 300M and the amino acid token embeddings are averaged into one 960-dimensional vector, so one protein is one token. The tokens are fed in genomic order into a 30-layer transformer of hidden size 960 that uses SwiGLU activations, rotary positional embeddings for order and learnable contig embeddings for chromosome and plasmid structure. Pretraining predicts the protein family of masked proteins out of 50 thousand clusters, while the input stays the exact protein sequence.

quotes.text: The transformer is 30 layer transformer with `hidden_dim=960` and is trained from scratch.
- Updated Transformer architecture: we use SwigLU activation function
The genomic organisation is highly important for bacteria, to model it we employ **rotary positional embeddings**
The contig embeddings are learnable embeddings which represent the unique contigs present in the genome.
the classification head predicts the protein family. We predict protein family, rather than a protein, because the space of possible proteins is effectively unbound.

sections.title: What distinguishes this size
sections.body: The card lists the differences from the base size: more than 300M parameters, SwiGLU activations, ESM-C 300M instead of ESM-2 as the base protein language model, no special tokens, and the forward argument renamed from token_type_ids to contig_ids. The Hugging Face safetensors index reports 431,765,841 parameters for both large checkpoints. The README says the release of Bacformer Large brought improved performance on downstream tasks.

quotes.text: Bacformer is a foundational model for bacterial genomics, modeling the whole bacterial genome as a sequence of proteins.
Each protein is treated as a token; thus, Bacformer may be viewed as a **contextualized protein language model**

facts.label: Architecture

run_guide.summary: Install the bacformer package and compute contextual protein embeddings with a Bacformer Large checkpoint.
prerequisites: Python 3.10, which the README names as the version Bacformer was developed in.
PyTorch 2.2 or above and flash attention, as the README install section asks for.
A CUDA GPU: the usage examples set device to cuda:0.
Network access to Hugging Face for the Bacformer Large checkpoint and the ESM-C base model.

steps.title: Embed a few protein sequences with Bacformer Large
steps.shell:
python3 - <<'PY'
import torch
from transformers import AutoModel
from bacformer.pp import protein_seqs_to_bacformer_inputs

device = "cuda:0"
model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(
    "macwiatrak/bacformer-large-masked-MAG", trust_remote_code=True
).to(device).eval().to(torch.bfloat16)

protein_sequences = [
    "MGYDLVAGFQKNVRTI",
    "MKAILVVLLG",
    "MQLIESRFYKDPWGNVHATC",
    "MSTNPKPQRFAWL",
]
inputs = protein_seqs_to_bacformer_inputs(
    protein_sequences,
    device=device,
    batch_size=128,
    max_n_proteins=6000,
    bacformer_model_type="large",
)

with torch.no_grad():
    outputs = model(**inputs, return_dict=True)
print('last hidden state shape:', outputs["last_hidden_state"].shape)
PY
steps.explanation: The README's Bacformer Large example, wrapped in a shell heredoc, with the comments removed.
